'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)]]
**[[2021 Afghanistan attacks]]
***Two guards are killed at a water dam near the [[Pashtun Kot District|Pashtun Kot]], [[Faryab Province|Faryab]], by the [[Taliban]]. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-news/taliban-attacks-security-outpost-near-dahandara-dam-in-afghanistan-101616938431096.html (''Hindustan Times'')]
***Over 20 civilians are killed in an [[military operation|operation]] launched by Afghan security forces against the [[Taliban]]. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/asia-pacific/afghanistan-civilians-killed-amid-anti-taliban-raid/2190870 (Anadolu Agency)]
***Three [[Afghan National Police|police]] officers are killed in a [[roadside bomb]] blast in [[Laghman Province|Laghman]]. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/asiapacific/2021-03/28/c_139842212.htm (Xinhuanet)]
***Five pro-government militia men are killed in an overnight attack in the [[Nangarhar Province]] in eastern Afghanistan. [https://www.thenews.com.pk/print/811565-five-pro-govt-militias-killed-in-eastern-afghanistan (''The News International'')]
*[[Terrorism in Indonesia]]
**[[2021 Makassar cathedral bombing]]
***Twenty people are wounded in a double [[suicide bombing]] outside the [[Sacred Heart Cathedral, Makassar|Sacred Heart Catholic Cathedral]] in [[Makassar]], [[South Sulawesi]], [[Indonesia]]. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asia/suspected-suicide-bomber-indonesia-church-injured-14509726 (CNA)]
*[[2021 Myanmar protests]]
**Myanmar's security forces open fire on a funeral being held for a person killed in [[Yangon]], with no casualties reported. The [[Kachin Independence Army]] also attacks a police station, prompting the [[Tatmadaw|military]] to conduct [[airstrike]]s. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-myanmar-politics/troops-fire-at-funeral-as-myanmar-mourns-bloodiest-day-since-coup-idUSKBN2BK00T?il=0 (Reuters)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Tencent Music]] announces that, starting tomorrow, it will [[Share repurchase|repurchase]] up to [[United States dollar|US$]]1 billion of its own stock over the next year in response to the [[U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission]] tightening its auditing standards for foreign firms listed on American [[stock exchange]]s. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-tencent-music-buyback/tencent-music-announces-biggest-ever-1-billion-share-buyback-idUSKBN2BL06X?il=0 (Reuters)]
'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Maharashtra]]
*****[[Maharashtra]] reports a record 40,414 new cases of [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours despite a nightly curfew, thereby bringing the total of confirmed cases to 2.71 million. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/with-40-414-covid-19-cases-maharashtra-records-highest-daily-infections-101616945265559-amp.html (''Hindustan Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mongolia]]
****[[Mongolia]] surpasses 7,000 cases of COVID-19. [https://www.marketwatch.com/press-release/mongolia-logs-321-new-covid-19-cases-total-tops-7000-2021-03-28?mod=news_archive (Marketwatch)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Pakistan]]
****The National Command and Operation Centre announces an immediate ban on all indoor and outdoor gatherings across [[Pakistan]] as well as weddings beginning April 5 due to an increase in the number of COVID-19 cases. [https://tribune.com.pk/story/2291921/indoor-outdoor-gatherings-banned-with-immediate-effect-ncoc (Tribune)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in North Macedonia]]
****[[North Macedonia]] receives their first shipment of 24,000 doses of the [[Oxford-AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford-AstraZeneca]] [[COVID-19 vaccine]] through the [[COVAX]] vaccine-sharing initiative. [https://www.unicef.org/northmacedonia/press-releases/north-macedonia-received-first-batch-covid-19-vaccine-covax-facility (UNICEF)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Slovenia]]
****[[Prime Minister of Slovenia|Prime Minister]] [[Janez Jansa]] announces a circuit-breaker [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] from April 1 to 12, which will close all non-essential businesses and in-person cultural and religious venues, ban gatherings of more than 10 people, and shift schools to [[remote learning]]. [https://english.sta.si/2884424/circuit-breaker-lockdown-to-be-imposed-from-1-april (STA)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in the United Kingdom]]
*****The number of people who have received their first dose of the [[COVID-19 vaccine]] in the [[United Kingdom]] surpasses 30 million. [https://news.sky.com/story/covid-19-uk-hits-30-million-first-vaccine-doses-12259255 (Sky News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Chile]]
***A lockdown begins across the entirety of [[Chile]], despite its successful [[vaccination]] programme, as the hospital occupancy rate reaches 95%. [https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2021/mar/28/chile-coronavirus-lockdowns-vaccination-success (''The Guardian'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico]]
***[[Mexico]] publishes revised figures, indicating that the number of deaths caused by COVID-19 is 60% higher than previously reported. The revised total is 321,000, thereby making it the country with the world's second-highest number of deaths. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-56558059 (BBC News)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/3/28/mexico-covid-death-toll-much-higher-than-previously-reported (Al Jazeera)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2019–2022 Sudanese transition to democracy]]
**The [[Sovereignty Council of Sudan|Sudanese transitional government]] and the [[Sudan People's Liberation Movement-North]] sign an agreement in the [[South Sudan]]ese capital of [[Juba]], holding that the new government will maintain the [[separation of church and state]] and uphold the [[freedom of religion|right to worship]] for all religions. [https://www.voanews.com/africa/sudan-rebel-group-sign-agreement-separation-religion-and-state (VOA)]
*[[Janikhel incident]]
**Thousands of protesters in Pakistan's [[Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]] province break through police barricades and attempt to march to [[Bannu]], and eventually reach [[Islamabad]], in order to demand a government probe into the deaths of four youths near [[Janikhel]]. The protesters allege that the youths were tortured and killed by [[Pakistan Armed Forces|security forces]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-pakistan-killings-protests/killing-of-youths-sparks-protests-in-northwest-pakistan-idUSKBN2BK0K2?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Dianne Feinstein]] becomes the longest serving [[United States Senate|U.S. Senator]] from [[California]], surpassing [[Hiram Johnson]]. [https://www.latimes.com/politics/story/2021-03-28/dianne-feinstein-becomes-californias-longest-serving-us-senator (''Los Angeles Times'')]
